symptom: The Shadow Evidence Draft 2020-12 countMap schema constrained only values, so a schema-only consumer admitted positive count-map entries named selection, sourceDecisionHistoryId, payoutYen or other private identifiers. The runtime validator already denied these names. Synthetic jsonschema Draft 2020-12 probes reproduced the schema-only gap; no private data or production impact was observed.
lesson: A sanitized count map with positive bounded integer values can still carry private identifier names. Schema-only consumers require a propertyNames denylist aligned with the runtime FORBIDDEN_KEYS; digest consistency and value bounds alone do not enforce key privacy.
guardrail: Retain Draft 2020-12 countMap.propertyNames.not.enum for the 12 runtime-forbidden identity and sensitive-field keys across unresolved, rejected and taxonomy dictionaries. Keep runtime path-token checks, semantic taxonomy reconciliation and content digest validation; this schema rule is a narrow lexical guardrail, not complete privacy attestation or external source authority.
